text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Mubarak calls for working teams to develop financial and banking institutions and communications sector. President meets members of the Egyptian-U.S. presidential council.
- Mubarak discusses stages of implementation of Hebron deal in telephone call with Arafat.

- World Bank ready to contribute to New Wadi project; parliament speaker Sorour tells National Democratic Party's political club that parliament will discuss law to give private sector right to build and manage airports.
- Russian envoy says after meeting Mubarak his country supports Egypt's efforts in peace process and that Russia will take part in New Wadi project.
- Defence Minister Tantawi says during 1973 war anniversary celebrations that job of armed forces during peace is harder than during war.
- Military court gives death sentences to four members of military wing of al-Gama'a al-Islamiyah.
- Supply Minister tells parliament there is no shortage of wheat and that imported meat is safe.
- New Wadi projects exempt from tax and customs duties.
- Stock exchange volume on Sunday was 85 million pounds.
- Sudanese oppositon National Democratic Alliance says Mubarak's comments on fighting in Sudan reflecs his deep understanding of crisis.
- Mobile telephones banned in exam halls.
- Court in Alexandria begins trying four policemen for beating man to death.
- Sudanese pressure on Egypt -- Turabi threatens to pull out troops that protect water in south.
